title: CPUNET subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_raw.c bt_buf_get_tx adoption (private pool pointers)

instruction_shape_match.dispatch: type==0 -> pool A; type==2 -> pool B; anything else -> LOG_ERR and return NULL
instruction_shape_match.abi: r0=type, r1=alignment hole, r2:r3=k_timeout_t, stack: data, size -- exactly bt_buf_get_tx(enum bt_buf_type, k_timeout_t, const void *, size_t)

private_state_defect.explanation: These are the ORIGINAL image's addresses of hci_raw.c's file-static hci_cmd_pool and hci_acl_pool, not an array base.  Iteration 18 bound the second one to _net_buf_pool_list_start, which happens to be correct only because hci_acl_pool is the FIRST pool in the linked net_buf_pool_area; the first one was left as a raw literal and in the iteration-19 net link 0x210009c8 falls inside the STOCK hci_rx_pool (0x21000998..0x210009cc).
private_state_defect.runtime_defect_observed: Every host->controller HCI command allocated from a net_buf_pool pointer aimed at the last 4 bytes of hci_rx_pool, corrupting the very pool bt_buf_get_evt() uses.  Measured: the app core's HCI Reset (0x0c03) reached the controller and the CPUNET then logged '<err> bt_sdc_hci_driver: No event buffer available' at t = 5.0938 s, so the Command Complete was never returned and bt_hci_cmd_send_sync() blocked forever.
